translation_notes: OWL_NS = Namespace('http://www.w3.org/2002/07/owl#') absorbed into '@prefix owl: <...> .'; the three namespace terms become prefixed names inside the graph.remove() tuples: RDFS.subClassOf -> rdfs:subClassOf, OWL_NS.equivalentClass -> owl:equivalentClass, OWL_NS.complementOf -> owl:complementOf

the mechanical draft named the prefix after the Python variable (owl-ns:), which is unusable outside g{} islands, and inserted the @prefix statements INSIDE the parenthesised 'from rdflib import (...)' list; both fixed by hand
only the prefixes actually used are declared; the draft also declared rdf: (unused in this region) merely because RDF is in the import list

context shim: infixowl_shim re-exports BooleanClass, CastClass, Class, Individual, classOrIdentifier and some from rdflib.extras.infixowl (rdflib 7.2.1), the maintained descendant of the vendored rdflib 3.x copy the region comes from -- the vendored copy imports rdflib.py3compat and no longer loads; imported identically by both sides

demo harness added identically to both sides: the region reads Individual.factoryGraph, a class-level attribute shared by the two runs, so it cannot be prepared by a driver fixture (run_pair builds both fixtures before calling either side); the harness replays the region's own docstring scenario at module level and leaves demo_graph for comparison. The docstring itself is kept verbatim, doctest markers included

finding: this region only *deletes* triples. graph.remove((s, p, None)) is a pattern-matching erase, and ldpy has no island for filtering or removal, so the statements keep their Python shape entirely -- the notation buys three prefixed names and nothing else. A g{}-shaped delete (or a removal pattern island) is the natural extension this example argues for
